authors: Tibshirani, R.J., Barber, R.F., Candes, E.J. & Ramdas, A.
title: Conformal prediction under covariate shift
source: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 32 (NeurIPS 2019) (arXiv:1904.06019)
relevance: Extends conformal beyond exchangeability to the case where train and test COVARIATE distributions differ, by reweighting calibration scores by the likelihood ratio - and states the ratio can be estimated from a large set of UNLABELLED test covariates. That is precisely our position: labels for one year, but 18 years of unlabelled imagery available to estimate how each year's imagery distribution differs from 2020. This is the mechanism that could carry a guarantee from a labelled year to an unlabelled one, and it is the single most directly usable result found in this loop so far.

authors: Barber, R.F., Candes, E.J., Ramdas, A. & Tibshirani, R.J.
title: Conformal prediction beyond exchangeability
relevance: The general non-exchangeable case, peer-reviewed: coverage still holds but degrades by an explicit, computable term measuring how far the data departs from exchangeability. This converts our 2000/2002 hard floor from 'unmeasurable' into 'measurable with a stated coverage penalty' - we could publish a bound and say honestly how much it is weakened by the temporal gap, instead of shipping LOW-CONFIDENCE with no number. Directly addresses open questions Q12 and Q13, and it is the theoretical licence for applying any of the Search 18 risk-control machinery across our non-exchangeable years.
